# Worked examples (sizing, risk budget, stops, funding)

Source-cited numbers; each block states the unit. Signs: this skill's convention (positive DV01 = long duration) unless a source is quoted in its own convention.

## 1. VaR-minimising trades (Darbyshire, Pricing and Trading Interest Rate Derivatives, 3rd ed., 2022)
Book in the source's sign (+ = paid), buckets 2Y / 5Y / 10Y / 30Y, daily bp^2 covariance Q = [[8.7, 7.4, 5.1, 2.2], [7.4, 7.3, 4.7, 2.2], [5.1, 4.7, 4.9, 1.8], [2.2, 2.2, 1.8, 1.9]] (9 daily changes in the text; use >= 100 in practice).
S = (-10,000, 2,500, 10,000, -4,000); c = 16,174 (book, unrounded Q; the rounded Q printed above gives ~16,400, so reproduce the method, not the last digit).

| Single-instrument VaR-minimising trade | trade | change in c | % of c |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2Y | +2,948 | -2,524 | 15.6% |
| 5Y | +2,304 | -1,247 | 7.7% |
| 10Y | -475 | -34 | 0.2% |
| 30Y | +3,373 | -688 | 4.1% |

Two-instrument minima: 2Y and 10Y (+8,562, -9,476) cuts c by 11,600 (just over 70%); 5Y and 10Y cuts 4,892; 2Y and 5Y 3,410. Euler allocation 15,787 / -2,602 / 1,437 / 1,552 (sum 16,174).
Reading: risk is a 2Y position; the 5Y leg is a diversifier and should not be cut; the best single hedge is only 15.6%, so a large part of the risk is RV risk.

Trader-level desk book (1Y..10Y, net delta 47k): c = 259, VaR_5% 425, VaR_1% 602. All ten par-bucket suggestions are receives (-29 to -96), cutting c by 14-26%: they only hedge directionality. A model book (spreads and flies) gives 2s5s10s -73 (25%), 5s7s10s -69 (11%), 3s4s5s +98 (10%). Executing ~50% of the top three (receive 30k 2Y, 35k 2s5s10s, 35k 5s7s10s) cut c from 259 to 175 (-33%), slightly more than any single trade; VaR_5% 287, VaR_1% 406.
Winner with ~0 VaR contribution (7s8s9s had the largest P&L and 0% VaR) is a take-profit candidate.

Directionality hedge of a 2s5s10s (-1, 2, -1): VaR-minimise only the 5Y amount -> weights proportional to (-1.17, 1.94, -1.17); minimise 2Y and 10Y -> (-1.43, 1.94, -0.37), lower VaR but far from the intended structure. More degrees of freedom reduce VaR and move the package away from its identity.

Desk aggregation: books with c = 336 and 291 combine to 529 versus the sum 627, so offsets were modest. Diversification arithmetic: n independent equal strategies give total risk sqrt(n) x each; Sharpe_portfolio = sqrt(n) x Sharpe_single (0.3 over 100 bets -> 3.0), capped by pairwise correlation.

VaR carry charge (manager charges 10% of VaR_5% as running cost): five independent strategies with c = 100k each (VaR_5% 164k) have E[PnL] 159,580. Charging drops the two with the lowest conviction (50%, 60%), leaving c 173.2k, VaR_5% 284.1k, E[PnL] 143,620. Use as a way to force low-conviction trades out of a shared budget.

## 2. Kelly arithmetic
- Single strategy (Chan, Quantitative Trading, 2009; equities used only for arithmetic): mean 11.23%, sd 16.91%, rf 4% -> excess 7.231%, Sharpe 0.4275, f = 0.07231 / 0.1691^2 = 2.528. Growth at Kelly g = r + S^2/2 = 13.14%; unlevered g = mu - s^2/2 = 9.8% (not 11.23%): variance drag. Half-Kelly 1.26, but the worst one-day loss 20.47% with a 20% tolerable one-day drawdown caps leverage at ~1, so min(half-Kelly, cap) = 1.
- Rebalancing: $252,800 position on $100k, price -10% -> position $227,520, equity $74,720 -> target 2.528 x 74,720 = $188,892 (sell into the loss). Kelly deleverage is pro-cyclical; hence half-Kelly and slow lookbacks (~6 months for 1-day holds).
- Three strategies: M = (0.1396, 0.0294, -0.0073), C = [[0.1109, 0.0200, 0.0183], [0.0200, 0.0372, 0.0269], [0.0183, 0.0269, 0.0420]] -> F = C^-1 M = (1.2919, 1.1723, -1.4882), g = 0.04 + F'CF/2 = 15.29%, Sharpe = sqrt(F'CF) = 0.4751. The third strategy has a negative mean excess return and is shorted.
- Parameter uncertainty (Paleologo, The Elements of Quantitative Investing, 2025): mu 0.08, sigma 0.19: plug-in mu/sigma^2 = 2.22, second-moment form mu/(mu^2 + sigma^2) = 1.88; tau_mu 0.04 -> 1.81; tau_sigma 0.1 -> 1.52. Mis-estimated Sharpe can bankrupt: vol 19%, SR 0.84 -> 4.4x. A per-period vol cap p gives x = min(p/sigma, SR): a constant vol-per-capital rule is a fractional Kelly (source's weekly example: cap 0.11 versus full-Kelly weekly SR 2/sqrt(52) = 0.27).
- Cantelli (Paleologo): annual SR 3, vol $50M, P(loss of $100M = 2 sd) <= 1/(1+(2+3)^2) = 3.85%, which the source rounds to 3.9%, versus 2.9e-7 under normality; use the bound as a distribution-free tail check, not a forecast.
- Classifier Kelly (J.P. Morgan, Do androids dream of electric bonds?, 22 Nov 2017): S = 2P - 1; the balanced random-forest strategy reached Sharpe 1.35 versus 0.38 all-long on a quarantined 2017 sample; hit rate saturated ~57% while Sharpe kept rising with conviction sizing; 10y bid/ask costs ~0.1 Sharpe.
- Forecast-scaled versus 1/0 (Salomon Brothers, Understanding the Yield Curve Part 4, Aug 1995): position proportional to predicted excess return gave average excess 8.64%, vol 12.80, Sharpe 0.68 versus 4.16 / 7.92 / 0.53 for hold-or-cash and 0.67 / 10.42 / 0.06 always-bond; transaction-intensive and the results are exaggerated by costs and shorting.

## 3. Strategy-risk binomial (Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning, 2018)
Symmetric payoffs +/-pi, precision p, n bets per year: SR = (2p - 1) / (2 sqrt(p(1-p))) x sqrt(n). p = 0.55 needs n = 396 bets/yr for SR 2; weekly bets need p = 0.6336. Asymmetric (pi+ = +0.5%, pi- = -1%, n = 260): SR = ((pi+ - pi-) p + pi-) / ((pi+ - pi-) sqrt(p(1-p))) x sqrt(n) = 1.173 at p = 0.70, 2.0 at p = 0.72, 0 at p = 2/3. Reject a strategy if P[p < p*] > 5% where p* is the break-even precision for the target Sharpe (estimate by bootstrap or N(p-bar, p-bar(1 - p-bar))). In low-payoff, high-frequency packages a 3-point precision error removes the profit.

## 4. OU stops and targets
- Optimal trading rule mesh (Lopez de Prado 2018): fit P_t = E0 + phi (P_{t-1} - E0) + noise by OLS, half-life tau = -log2 / log(phi); simulate 100,000 paths, max holding ~100 observations, profit-take 0.5-10 sigma x stop-loss 0.5-10 sigma; pick max Sharpe. Zero equilibrium, tau = 5: small PT with wide SL best (SR ~3.2); tight SL with wide PT worst; symmetric ~ neutral. Positive equilibrium: tau 5 -> PT ~6, SL 4-10, SR ~12; tau 10 -> SR ~9; tau 25 -> PT ~3, SL 9-10, SR 2.7; tau 50 -> SR 0.8; tau 100 -> 0.32 and no optimum (a flat heat-map: any chosen stop is overfitted).
- First-passage design (Huggins & Schaller, Fixed Income Relative Value Analysis, 2nd ed., 2024): dx = k(mu - x) dt + v dw with k = 0.30, mu = 20, v = 20, start 40bp, 10,000 paths answers "chance of a stop at 55bp in 2 weeks", "stop giving a 20% hit chance in a month", "chance to reach a 35bp target in 2 months", expected time to the mean. The expected path never reaches the mean but expected first-passage time is finite. Annualised ex-ante Sharpe falls with holding horizon under OU (4-week 0.76 -> 2.73 annualised): short horizons, tight targets (half the distance), stop at the moving 2 sd band. Caveat: vol is often higher far from the mean, so constant-vol OU overstates Sharpe at extreme entries.
- Leung & Li (Optimal Mean Reversion Trading, 2016): three regions (take-profit, delay, stop); if the stop L >= L* = (mu theta + r c_s)/(mu + r) (about the mean), liquidate at once; b_L* falls as L rises (tighter stop lowers the take-profit); enter only inside [a_L*, d_L*] above L; stop example L = theta - 2 sigma / sqrt(2 mu). Holding penalty q is equivalent to lowering the exit cost to c_s - q/r (take profit sooner). Their cost example is internally inconsistent, so treat their numeric levels as illustrative.
- Practice: ING EUR 2s5s10s PC1-neutral fly (weights -2.41 / +2 / -0.66, 50% risk allocation): entry 49.5bp (0.5bp charge from 50 mid), target 20, stop 65 -> reward 29.5 / risk 15.5 = 1.9; carry and roll 4.7bp/3m; downside bounded by an extreme-curve scenario of ~10bp for belly receivers (ING, 9 Mar 2020).
- Citi model portfolio (Macro tapas, 7 Aug 2026): 229 trades since 2023, 51% in profit, +24.8% of the $100mm portfolio. Closed examples (DV01, move, P&L; the first three P&Ls do not equal DV01 x move because of carry, rebalancing or DV01 drift, so use them as outcomes, not as arithmetic): Dec26/Dec27 FF OIS steepener 50k 10.5 -> -0.9bp -$942k; USD OIS 2s10s steepener 45k 24 -> 10.78 -$582k; pay NOK vs receive SEK 12x15 FRA 15k 164.5 -> 249.6 +$580k. Radar trade 1y-forward 5s30s steepener 50k DV01 at 75.5bp, stop 30bp of flattening, now 42.3bp = 33bp flattening, beyond the stop, -$1,662k: a stop that is not executed is not a stop. Return on risk convention: P&L / largest two-week change since Jan 1997 on a $300mm model portfolio (Citi, US Rates Weekly, 18 Jan 2019).

## 5. Funding and margin cases
- Margin trap (Aikin, Welcome to STIR futures forum): 3-month STIR calendar, 1 tick = $25 per spread, initial margin ~$160 -> $1M "holds" > 6,000 spreads = $150k per tick = 15% of capital. VaR sizing instead: sigma ~1 tick over a 3-month window, 99% VaR = 2.33 ticks, risk budget 5% of $1M = $50k -> 50,000 / (2.33 x 25) = ~850 spreads. Refinements: use 1M / 3M / 6M windows; err lower because several spreads are the same trade; liquidity is best in the 3m white and red packs.
- SPAN (Aikin, STIR Futures, 2012): 16 price/vol scenarios give the scanning risk; inter-month spread charge (Euribor tier 1: EUR 250 against EUR 850 outright); Euribor against a short 2y Swapnote (EUR 850 + EUR 600) each gets a 65% credit. A calendar spread is margined at ~25% of outright risk but many ISV risk systems count it as two outrights: check what the limit system counts. Rogue-trading cases (10,128 lots against a 50-lot limit) show limit enforcement matters.
- March 2020 Treasury basis (Tuckman & Serrat, Fixed Income Securities, 4th ed., 2022): $1bn long CTD basis at -8.33 ticks (6 Mar), hedge 7,978 futures; net basis moved -8.33 -> -18.48 on 9 Mar -> -0.47 on 12 Mar. Daily P&L -3.17mm / +2.27mm / +1.73mm / +1.63mm; margin per contract 1,275 -> 1,600; margin calls 0.80mm (9 Mar) and 1.79mm (11 Mar). Target ~$2.5mm, yet on 9 Mar ~$3.2mm loss + ~$0.8mm margin = ~$4mm cash in one day, enough to trigger a loss limit or forced exit although the trade later converged. 99th-percentile repo minus SOFR: 10-11bp in Feb 2020, 20-50bp several March days, 174bp on 16 Mar. Daily closes understate intraday vol. Leverage: 20:1 on $50mm capital ~6.5% annualised over 141 days; 40:1 ~13%.
- Leveraged basis fund simulation (Burghardt et al., The Treasury Bond Basis, 3rd ed., 2005): 5 trades/yr, 5 ticks average, sd 8.6, worst/best = +/-2 sd, bills 6.5%: 25:1 -> average 26.0%, worst -4.0%, best 56.1%; 20:1 (recommended) 22.1% / -1.9% / 46.2%; 10:1 14.3% / +2.3% / 26.3%. Practical max ~25x cash, set by exchange margin and repo cash needs. Squeeze controls: watch declining special rate, large short sales, spread to similar issues; use a stop since "theoretically there is no maximum loss on a squeezed basis short".
- MF Global RTM (Tuckman & Serrat 2022): positions peaked at $11.5bn (June 2011) against a $4.75bn risk-manager limit sized for 15% haircuts; IE/PT haircuts 3% -> 80% in July 2011; margin rose from 2.9% to 10.6% of positions by Oct 2011; liquidation loss > $400mm. Had the position been sized for haircut stress it might have profited. Hedging price risk with reverse positions did not hedge the haircut risk.
- London Whale (same; a CDS book, used here only for the size-versus-ADV lesson): net notional $51bn end-2011 -> gross $157.1bn end-Mar 2012; position > 10 days ADV (one series > 8x ADV); cumulative loss $5.8bn through June 2012. Exiting cost estimates: $25bn RWA cut $400-590mm; 25-35% pro-rata cut > $500mm.
- Balance sheet ROE (Boyarchenko et al., Negative Swap Spreads, FRBNY, Oct 2018): $10mm 10y swap-spread widener, net carry $37,490, equity = SLR x (gross notional + haircut + IM + PFE) (PFE add-on 0% <= 1y, 0.5% 1-5y, 1.5% > 5y): equity $107,300 at 1% SLR up to $643,800 at 6%, ROE 35 / 17 / 12 / 9 / 7 / 6%. Breakeven 10y spread for 15% ROE at 5% SLR = -54bp versus +11bp pre-regulation.
- Margin offsets (Coalition Greenwich, Q4 2024; hypothetical maxima): 2y receive SOFR futures versus swap 1,558 -> 349 (78%); 10y UST futures versus swap 6,630 -> 2,646 (60%); 30y 12,924 -> 6,496 (50%). Real books get less; use a what-if margin calculator before sizing.

## 6. Risk-aversion calibration (Grinold & Kahn, 1999)
omega* = IR/(2 lambda), VA* = IR^2/(4 lambda). Risk (%) by IR and lambda 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.15: IR 1.0 -> 10 / 5 / 3.33; IR 0.75 -> 7.5 / 3.75 / 2.5; IR 0.5 -> 5 / 2.5 / 1.67. Value added: IR 1.0 -> 5.00 / 2.50 / 1.67; IR 0.5 -> 1.25 / 0.63 / 0.42. Implied aversion from a target: lambda = IR / (2 psi*) (IR 0.5, psi 5% -> 0.05). Calibration anchors (before fees): IR 90th percentile 1.0, 75th 0.5, median 0.0; IC good 0.05, great 0.10, world-class 0.15. Fundamental law IR ~ IC x sqrt(BR); independent sources add in squares (0.75, 0.50, 0.30 -> 0.95). Proof of skill takes ~16 years at IR 0.5; 20 tries give a 64% chance of a t >= 2 fluke.
Timing bet: beta* = delta f / (2 lambda_BT sigma^2); expected value added T x IC^2 / (4 lambda_BT).
Return forecasts barely change risk forecasts: sigma_post = sigma_prior sqrt(1 - IC^2). Constraints shrink effective skill (in the book's example, constraints cut the IC by 62%); make the cost explicit.
